claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you are looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. I have a few questions about Alex and your circumstances to help determine your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, I need to ask about his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or on an approved training course? (This would include things like A-levels, T-levels, Scottish Highers, or a government-approved training scheme, but not higher education like university or a paid apprenticeship.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

When you say Alex has "signed up with the local careers service," could you clarify what this involves? Specifically, is he registered with a qualifying body (such as the Careers Service in Northern Ireland, a local careers service, or Connexions) for education or training, and is he either:

- Waiting to start a place on an approved education or training course, or
- Actively being considered for a place on such a course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He registered with them recently and they're helping him find a course or training program to start. He's waiting to get onto something suitable.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. It sounds like Alex is registered with a qualifying careers service and is waiting to start a course or training program, which is relevant for eligibility.

I have a couple more questions:

How long ago did Alex leave school, and has he been registered with the careers service for the entire time since leaving? (Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education if the young person registers with a careers service within a certain timeframe.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school not too long ago, and he registered with the careers service pretty much right away. It's been within those 20 weeks you mentioned.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question about Alex: Does he live with you, and are you responsible for him? (This means you're the person mainly responsible for looking after him day-to-day.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me and I look after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I just need to ask a couple of questions about your own circumstances.

Are you aged 16 or over?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one final question:

Do you live in the UK? (This includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:
- You are over 16 and live in the UK
- Alex is 17 years old and lives with you
- You are responsible for looking after him
- He recently left school and registered with a local careers service right away
- He is waiting to start an approved education or training course
- It has been within the 20-week period since he left education

Based on the eligibility rules, you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. The rules allow Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a qualifying careers service, which Alex has done.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ You are over 16 and live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you and you are responsible for him
- ✅ Although Alex is 17 and has left school, he registered with a local careers service promptly after leaving
- ✅ He is waiting to start an approved education or training course
- ✅ It has been within the 20-week extension period

**Important to note:** This eligibility can continue for up to 20 weeks from when Alex left education, as long as he remains registered with the careers service and is waiting for a place on a course or training. Once he either starts an approved course (in which case eligibility may continue until he's 20), or the 20-week period ends without him starting a course, you would need to reassess eligibility.

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, please feel free to ask!
